pill.desc: pale-yellow to brownish-yellow solution in a single-dose vial

tell: A taxoid semisynthesized from a precursor extracted from yew needle biomass.

clues.text: It is about 94% protein bound in vitro, and fecal excretion is the main elimination route, with about 75% of radioactivity recovered within 7 days.
Molecular weight 807.9 for the parent compound. It is highly lipophilic and practically insoluble in water.
Approved under an NDA as a one-vial injection at 20 mg/mL, in 20 mg and 80 mg single-dose vials. Given every 3 weeks.

Boxed warning for toxic deaths, hepatotoxicity, neutropenia, hypersensitivity and fluid retention. Contraindicated with severe hypersensitivity to the drug or polysorbate 80; anemia and neutropenia are common.

Breast cancer, as a single agent after chemotherapy failure or as adjuvant therapy with doxorubicin and cyclophosphamide; non-small cell lung cancer; and castration-resistant prostate cancer with prednisone.

Binds free tubulin and promotes assembly into stable microtubules while inhibiting their disassembly, so mitosis is inhibited. Unlike most spindle poisons, it does not alter the number of protofilaments.
The generic name begins with D and has nine letters.
